newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's bellwether Cetes rate up on peso weakness.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's bellwether Cetes rate up on peso weakness.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate rose on Tuesday at the primary treasury bill auction in reaction to a weaker peso, analysts said.
At the Banco de Mexico primary auction, the 28-day paper rate rose 164 basis points to 29.34 percent.
"It was an increase in reaction to volatility in the exchange (market). It was totally to support the peso," said Ricardo Vazquez, an analyst with Banco Union.
The Mexican peso has weakened recently. The spot 48-hour unit closed 3.6 centavos weaker at 7.935/7.94 per dollar on Tuesday.
The Mexican currency has weakened partially on concerns it might be overvalued. Money market rates have risen to support the weakening currency.
Primary interest rates responded to pressures in the secondary money market, where the rate on overnight paper on Tuesday rose above 30 percent at one point before closing at 28.60 percent.

According to a Reuters' survey of 10 Cetes dealers on Tuesday, interest rate on the bellwether 28-day Cetes was seen rising 141 basis points to 29.11 percent, and longer term rates were also seen rising.
The slightly larger than expected rise in one-month paper should help control speculation against the peso, analysts said.
"The levels are sufficiently high and with the economic policies for next year practically defined, rates should have reached a short-term ceiling," said Vazquez.
On Tuesday, the 91-day Cetes were assigned at 30.10 percent, 131 basis points higher than last week. The 181-day paper was assigned at 29.30 percent, 49 basis points higher.
The 336-day paper was assigned at 28.63 percent, while last week 343-day paper was assigned at 28.41 percent, Banco de Mexico said.

Another factor in the hike in rates was the decline in demand, which fell to 10.01 billion pesos this week from 12.15 billion last week, analysts said. There were 3.3 billion pesos on auction this week.
"The decline in demand reflects a cautious tone by investors after the release of the (government, business and labour) economic package," said another analyst.
On the weekend the so-called Alliance for Economic Growth released its economic package for 1997.
The government, business and labour alliance called for growth of four percent next year and inflation of 15 percent.
